results.title: Gateway trusts the IdP CA (spec OSG-TLS-03 chain)
results.desc: SA JWTs issued by private-PKI keycloak validate at the gateway
results.prose: Random spec draw (third honest hit on the TLS spec — this time OSG-TLS-03, the CA-bundle injection for private-PKI IdPs). The reconciler half (ConfigMap copy, /etc/pki mount, SSL_CERT_FILE) isn't visible from a sandbox, but the end-to-end proof is: our SA JWTs are issued by keycloak.hyp2 over TLS protected by the same OpenShell Sandbox CA we saw on the routes — and the gateway validates those tokens on every authenticated RPC. A gateway missing its CA bundle would reject all OIDC tokens; ours accepts them all cycle. The trust chain the spec builds is functioning.
results.steps: rpc ListSandboxes with SA bearer (token minted from the private-PKI keycloak); grpc=0 proves gateway-side CA trust + token validation.

results.title: Gateway version stability (longitudinal)
results.desc: Same gateway version across every cycle since Nov 6
results.prose: A longitudinal observation worth pinning in the catalog: this gateway has served every cycle since November 6 on version 0.1.6-rhaiv.2 — no upgrades, no restarts visible from the API surface, while the fleet around it (per the Nov 8 listing) runs seven versions including newer rhaiv.4 builds. Our test surface has been stable, which makes the catalog's pass/fail history directly comparable across all 32 runs.
